decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach to standing green bottle, keeping right arm parked and using small elbow-up-continuous increments.
Replan from interrupted pose with reduced translation increments toward the green bottle.
Advance open left gripper toward the green bottle body; account for link6-to-finger offset.
Fine-align left fingers around green bottle using wrist view; remain open until body is centered.
Close left gripper on the centered green bottle, then lift a short distance to visually check retention.
Carry the green bottle leftward with gripper held closed, checking that it follows the hand toward the bin.
Green bottle did not follow the hand. Reopen and approach again, farther forward so the fingers surround rather than stop before the body.
Bottle is now lying down. Lift clear and begin a downward-facing grasp approach, maintaining configuration continuity.
Continue turning the left fingers downward while advancing above the near half of the lying green bottle.
Align downward-facing fingers over the green bottle's near body and lower gradually; grasp remains open.
Use millimeter corrections after the continuity guard, close over the green bottle's near end, and test retention with a small lift.
Lift and retract leftward with the gripper closed to verify capture, gradually reducing downward wrist tilt and reach.
No retention seen. Reopen and lower the downward-pointing fingers substantially toward the lying bottle's near body; previous attempt was above it.
Fine forward/down correction around the green bottle's lower body, then close without lifting yet.
Keep closing, then gently lift and retract to check whether the green bottle is retained between the fingers.
Green bottle appears to follow the fingers. Lift and move toward the left bin with the gripper kept closed.
Carry the retained green bottle left and back toward the bin, keeping it above the rim and maintaining a closed grip.
Position the whole green bottle over the bin opening before releasing; keep the grip closed during transport.
Move the green bottle clear of the bin's far rim, open the left gripper to drop it, and lift away slightly.
Green bottle is visibly inside the bin. Retract the left arm and begin a cautious right-arm approach to the standing white bottle.
Continue toward the standing white bottle with the right hand, clearing the lying bottles; bring the left hand back toward a safe receiving position.
Advance the open right fingers toward the white bottle at body height, with a small leftward alignment correction.
Insert right fingers the last few centimeters around the standing white bottle, then close and pause before lifting.
Allow the right gripper to finish closing, then lift the white bottle a short distance to verify retention.
White bottle follows the right hand. Raise it toward a central handover while orienting the open left hand to receive from its own side.
Bring the bottle to the center-right and orient the left fingers toward its upper body for handover, keeping the right grasp closed.
Align the open left fingers with the white bottle's upper shoulder while the right hand holds the lower body stationary.
Seat the white bottle's upper body between the left fingers and close the receiving grip, keeping the right grip closed during transfer.
Receiving fingers appear above/off-center on the white bottle. Reopen and correct slightly forward and lower onto its shoulder before reclosing; right hand continues holding.
Test the receiving grasp: keep the left hand closed, open and withdraw the right hand, then make a small left lift to check retention visually.
The white bottle was not retained by the left hand and is now on the table. Clear the left hand and reorient the right for a top-down regrasp.
Replan the rejected rotation with smaller wrist and translation increments; left hand clears the regrasp area.
Continue the right-hand downward approach above the lying white bottle, keeping the left hand clear and both grippers open.
The white bottle is right of the downward-facing fingers. Translate right to center its body between the open jaws before closing.
Lift the right fingers clear before lateral alignment; the previous low sideways approach slid the bottle rather than surrounding it.
Center the right fingers above the lying white bottle and descend vertically around its near body, avoiding sideways pushing at table height.
Make a small centering correction, close the right fingers around the white bottle, and test with a short lift while the left arm stays clear.
White bottle remains on the table. Reopen and lower the right fingers below the bottle's midline before closing again.
Finish closing and lift the white bottle with a small leftward retreat to verify that it follows the right hand.
Reopen; account for the downward tool offset and lower to the bottle's actual table-level body, with small forward and right corrections.
Close at table level with the white bottle visibly between the fingers, then lift slowly to verify capture.
White bottle is now retained. Raise and rotate it so its free neck points toward the left workspace, preparing a downward receiving grasp without crossing arms.
Reduce left wrist rotation substantially after the continuity rejection. Continue lifting and turning the retained bottle toward the center.
Continue turning the bottle's free end leftward and gradually pitch the receiving fingers down, preserving the successful right grasp.
Lower and seat the left fingers around the white bottle's free shoulder, then close while the right hand remains stationary and closed.
White bottle is visibly seated in both grips. Open and separate the right hand, keeping the left closed, then test retention with a small lift and leftward move.
Transfer did not retain the bottle; it is now on the central table. Clear the right hand and prepare a downward left-hand grasp on its accessible neck/shoulder.
Align the open left fingers with the white bottle's neck and descend toward its table-level shoulder, keeping the right hand clear.
Close the left fingers on the centered white shoulder, then lift vertically a short distance to check whether the bottle is retained.
White bottle remains on the table. Reopen and lower the left fingers to the actual shoulder midline, correcting slightly forward rather than closing above it.
At contact height, stop descending and close on the white bottle's neck; lift gently to distinguish capture from table contact.
Reopen and advance along the bottle toward the wider shoulder, rather than pinching just above the narrow neck; then close in place.
Hold the left grip closed and lift the white shoulder away from the table to verify retention before carrying it to the bin.
The white bottle was not retained. Reorient to a more vertical top-down left grasp over the shoulder, clearing the table before descending.
Descend the nearly vertical open left fingers around the white bottle shoulder, correcting the small lateral offset seen in the wrist view.
Close the vertical left grasp at shoulder height, allow closure to settle, then lift straight up to verify retention.
Lift and retract the closed left grasp to clear the white bottle from the table and verify that it follows before moving over the bin.
White bottle follows the left grasp. Carry it toward the bin and turn its free end away from the table while maintaining a closed grip.
Continue carrying the retained white bottle over the bin, keeping its free end clear of the table and the grasp closed.
Release the white bottle over the bin. Begin an open right-hand approach above the peach bottle, keeping the left hand away.
White bottle is visibly in the bin. Lower the right fingers around the peach bottle and close; return the left hand toward a safe receiving approach.
Lift the peach bottle with the right grip closed and bring it toward center-right; restore the left hand's downward receiving orientation without crossing arms.
Bring the peach bottle's free end toward the center and approach it from above with the left fingers, keeping the right grasp closed.
Advance the left downward fingers over the peach bottle's free end and close, while the right hand maintains the supported bottle position.
The hands are close with contact residuals. Hold the left grasp stationary, open the right grip and withdraw it gently to test the handover without squeezing the hands together.
The peach bottle fell onto the central table. Reopen and lower the left top-down grasp onto its accessible cap/body while moving the right arm clear.
Close the left fingers around the peach bottle at table level and lift vertically to check retention before transport.
Peach bottle was not retained. Reopen, advance onto the wider body beyond the cap, and lower a little further for a deeper top-down grasp.
Correct the peach bottle's lateral offset seen in the wrist view, lifting slightly before recentering and closing at contact height.
Keep the left grasp closed and lift the peach bottle gently, beginning a small leftward retreat to verify retention.
Peach bottle slipped. Reopen and target farther along its body, using a slightly shallower downward angle and a deeper approach rather than gripping the end cap.
Center the peach body within the left jaw gap with a small lateral correction, lower slightly, and close without lifting yet.
Lift the centered peach bottle with the left grip closed and retreat toward the left, checking that it follows the fingers.
